summary: Round 2 of dow-trend-classification resolves all six round-1 findings and introduces no regressions. Verified fixes: Example 2 now lists the 2020-04-08 DEFENSE_BREAK and its Reading explains the BEAR_SUSPECT episode with dates that match a fresh ClickHouse run (reaction high 23185.62 from the 2020-03-13 swing, HL counter swing of 2020-06-26 confirmed 2020-08-05); the abbreviation note matches the rows shown. The new skill-local fixture tests/fixtures/defense_break_sample.csv is reproduced byte for byte by its generator, and running the wrapper on it gives exactly the sequence the test asserts (strict: HL, HH, TREND_ESTABLISHED, DEFENSE_BREAK 2021-04-29 now suspect, LL, LH, REVERSAL_DOWN 2021-06-22, LL, since 2021-06-22; non-strict: the same minus the REVERSAL, flip on the break, since 2021-04-29), a truncation at 2021-05-05 leaves BULL_SUSPECT with the broken line, and a ClickHouse-gated test checks the ^DJI 2015 run for the 2018-12-19 and 2020-04-08 breaks, the 2023-06-15 REVERSAL_UP and the 45166.64 line. The 597-session stall is now attributed to the review's secondary_pct 0.10 configuration in Example 3, Limitations 2 and evidence.md; the Step 1 table has no Chinese terms and references dow-swing-detection Step 4 instead of restating the zig-zag; the preamble says 42 notes with the registry's 43 noted; the description trigger is narrowed to the primary trend and how the scales feed it. Re-run results: skill pytest 8 passed (the ClickHouse test executed, not skipped), check_labels.py and check_quotes.py ALL CLEAN, ruff check and ruff format --check pass on all seven Python files, no absolute paths, wrapper still 58 lines. Section order, labels, R-018 dual presentation, R-045 agent-defined provenance sentence, the R1 caveat and every previously verified quote and figure are unchanged. A careful domain expert can sign off; the remaining caveats (one-average machine, in-sample thresholds, thin reversal evidence) are stated in Limitations and are properties of the project, not of the skill text.
